editorial.headline: Financial-Market Clearing: Nationally Open, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers clearing and settlement across financial markets, with national foreign ownership open to 100% but PMA registration blocked for a Bali address.
editorial.body:
This activity sits behind the completion of financial-market transactions: it covers clearing and settlement for securities, commodity contracts, money-market and foreign-exchange transactions, digital financial assets, and other financial-market dealings. In plain terms, its subject is the process by which those transactions are cleared and settled across the markets named in the record. That breadth matters. The activity is defined by this transaction-completion function, rather than by one asset class alone.

Registration is open at every scale recorded—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes scale an inclusive national entry point in the record, not a narrow label reserved for a single size of business. Yet the Bali assessment adds a crucial qualification within that same record: the Besar scale is classed as Menengah Rendah for the relevant local assessment. The label matters because it is the classification to which the Bali PMA restriction attaches.

Nationally, the position is TERBUKA, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. A foreign investor therefore has a nationally open route to this activity under the stated national basis, Perpres 10/2021 and 49/2021. Bali is different. The activity is marked CHIUSO_MORATORIA_BALI and blocked for PMA registration at a Bali address. The record explains that the Bali PMA moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI island-wide and permanently; for this activity, the recorded Menengah Rendah assessment brings that block into force.

That is the decision-critical reading for a founder considering a Bali address. The national 100% ceiling does not override the local result: today, a foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali. Nor does the availability of Mikro through Besar change the stated moratorium outcome. The record presents national openness and Bali closure as two separate facts that must be read together. The precise conclusion is simple: nationally open, yet unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the permanent island-wide moratorium recorded here.
